messages:
pagerduty-bot: P0 — GeoDNS inconsistency detected: multiple users reporting 502s in eu-west and ap-southeast. Alert: external-dns-checks > 90% divergent answers between Cloudflare and Route53. Paging maya (oncall).

maya: grabbing it. any customer-facing impact flagged?

support_lead: yes — support saw a spike in 502s and some customers in EU complaining about model timeouts. Not wide but repeated for ~15m. Ticket #INC-9012.

sam (oncall): i'm awake, standing by for context. maya, do we have a quick blamestack?

maya: initial look — authoritative answers from our Cloudflare geodns layer are returning older A records in multiple EU resolvers, while Route53 answers are the expected new set. looks like propagation + resolver cache divergence, but it's too focused in eu-west/APAC to be pure TTL.

ajay: running multi-region dig now.

ajay: dig outputs (from 3 probes):
```
; probe eu-west-1
;; ANSWER SECTION:
example.redwood.ai.  300 IN A 10.11.12.13  ; (stale)
; probe eu-west-3
;; ANSWER SECTION:
example.redwood.ai.  30 IN A 52.23.34.45  ; (expected)
; probe ap-southeast-1
;; ANSWER SECTION:
example.redwood.ai.  300 IN A 10.11.12.13  ; (stale)
```

liam: hmm. Cloudflare edge seems to be returning a cached older RRset in a subset of PoPs. Route53 good. Could be CF cache invalidation not fully propagated or an upstream sync problem in our workers.

maya: immediate mitigation options: 1) lower TTL on Route53 to force resolvers to refresh (but many resolvers respect cached TTL), 2) attempt a Cloudflare cache purge for the record (we have a purge API), 3) add a temporary CNAME to a canonical host that bypasses the bad CF cache via Route53-only routing, 4) fail traffic to Route53-only LBR.

sam (oncall): what's fastest to reduce customer impact?

liam: purge CF cache for the record first, then lower Route53 TTL to 60s. Purge should be quick but some CF PoPs still holding. Also recommend turning on Route53 geo-failover to prefer Route53 answers for EU while CF completes invalidation.

maya: executing purge now. calling Cloudflare API:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<zone>/purge_cache" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  --data '{"files":["https://example.redwood.ai/"]}'
```

sre-bot: purge request accepted (request_id=pf-8a1f).

ajay: starting distributed probes every 30s and logging responses.

support_lead: notifying impacted customers with temporary guidance: "We're seeing DNS inconsistencies in some regions; our engineering team is actively mitigating. If you see stale IPs, flush local resolver or try again in ~1-2 minutes. We'll update here."

20m later

ajay: probes show CF answers decreasing but still ~25% of eu-west PoPs returning old A. Route53 answers stable.

maya: route change: update Route53 TTL to 60 and create a Route53-only weighted record set to push traffic to the correct endpoint in EU while CF finishes. executing now.

liam: adding note — when we create a Route53-weighted record the global authoritative graph will still include both providers, but most resolvers will prefer the shorter TTL answers from Route53. This is a stopgap.

maya: TTL change done (old 300 -> 60). weighted record created with weight 100 for correct IPs.

sam (oncall): confirm dig from eu-west shows updated TTL and expected IP?

ajay: dig eu-west now:
```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
example.redwood.ai.  60 IN A 52.23.34.45
```

support_lead: support reporting reduction in tickets, customer timeouts down ~80% in EU. good.

sre-bot: Cloudflare reported internal cache purge success in zone pf-8a1f at +00:04. Some edge nodes still had propagation delay.

maya: next steps: monitor probes for 30-60m. if stable, revert weighted record and set TTL back to 300 after 1 hour. open postmortem to track root cause and CF edge stale cache mechanism.

liam: optional: request CF support to trace which PoPs had stale cache and why purge didn't affect them; might be an internal CF invalidation queue issue. I'll open the CF ticket and include packet captures and dig logs.

sam (oncall): agreed. I'll take a log of customer impact and add to incident timeline. Handoff: i'm staying on until 02:00 UTC; maya, if you need follow-up after that ping oncall@redwood.

maya: i'll continue monitoring for 45m, then hand off to night oncall if stable. documenting timeline here.

40m later

ajay: probes stable, CF answers now 99% correct. No new support tickets in last 20m.

support_lead: sending out customer update: "Issue largely mitigated. We performed cache invalidation and temporary routing adjustments. We're continuing to monitor and will notify when fully resolved."

maya: rolling back weighted record and raising TTL to 300.

liam: rollback complete. please let support know TTL propagation may take up to 5m for fresh resolvers.

sre-bot: incident closed for now (incident_id=INC-9012). follow-up owners: liam (CF ticket), ajay (probe dashboards), maya (postmortem writeup).

sam (oncall): handing off: maya -> night oncall at 02:00 UTC if anything reappears. I captured metrics and included dig samples in the incident doc.

maya: thanks all. postmortem checklist: timeline, CF purge effectiveness, resolver behavior analysis, consider adding automated cross-provider sanity checks and an automated ability to prefer one provider per-region during anomalies. I'll draft and circulate. :memo:

support_lead: closing the customer ticket with a follow-up summary.

pagerduty-bot: reminder — please label incident INC-9012 with "geo-dns" and "cloudflare" for analytics.

maya: done. moving to postmortem phase.
